mappings.note: Which language the rustic cart-driver understands (the heart's). Comprehension of the prose passage's content, so C-H2.3-LO-1 rather than C-H2.3-LO-2, which is for the writer's मंतव्य and भाषा-शैली.
Into whose soul Raj Kapoor's persona sank (Hiraman's). A fact of the essay, hence C-H2.3-LO-1 and not LO-2.
Who was established as Asia's greatest showman (Raj Kapoor). Content recall, so C-H2.3-LO-1.
How Raj Kapoor reacted to Shailendra's offer. Narrative content of the essay, so C-H2.3-LO-1 rather than LO-2.
The effect on Shailendra of the advance being asked for. An event in the essay, hence C-H2.3-LO-1.
What Raj Kapoor asked as his fee (one rupee). Factual recall, so C-H2.3-LO-1 and not LO-2.
Raj Kapoor's view of Shailendra as a producer (no commercial sense). A stated fact of the essay -- it is a character's opinion, not the writer's मंतव्य, so C-H2.3-LO-1 rather than LO-2.
Meaning of 'पारिश्रमिक' (= मेहनताना). A gloss on the text's diction, which falls on the भाषा side of C-H2.3-LO-2; C-H2.2 would need a grammar operation, not a शब्दार्थ.
Which film is Raj Kapoor's finest in acting terms (तीसरी कसम). Content recall, so C-H2.3-LO-1.
Which character Raj Kapoor merged with (हीरामन). A fact of the essay, C-H2.3-LO-1 rather than LO-2.
Which film did full justice to the literary work. Content recall, so C-H2.3-LO-1.
Who played the lead pair (Raj Kapoor and Waheeda Rehman). Factual, hence C-H2.3-LO-1.
What the characters were named (हीरामन and हीराबाई). Content recall, C-H2.3-LO-1 and not LO-2.
Which quality makes the film distinctive (tender feeling and innocence). The stem asks about the film, not about the writer's own view or style, so C-H2.3-LO-1 rather than LO-2.
Which language all the world's words cannot express (the eyes'). A statement retrieved from the passage, so C-H2.3-LO-1; items that name the लेखक's view are LO-2.
The greatest weakness of our films (absence of लोक-तत्त्व). Recalled from the passage without the लेखक being named, so C-H2.3-LO-1 -- the twin item phrased 'लेखक के अनुसार' is mapped LO-2.
What the lurid display of grief does to viewers (emotional exploitation). Content of the passage, so C-H2.3-LO-1.
The special quality of 'तीसरी कसम' (it presents sorrow in its natural, life-related state). Content recall, hence C-H2.3-LO-1.
What quality the लेखक attributes to Shailendra's songs. The stem asks for the writer's appraisal, which is exactly C-H2.3-LO-2 rather than LO-1's content recall.
What gives a person the message to move forward (व्यथा). Content of the passage, so C-H2.3-LO-1.

Same leading question as the preceding item, mapped C-H2.3-LO-1 on that content. Its stem has swallowed a long block of textbook Q&A, its key contradicts its twin's and its answer field holds an unrelated passage -- all reported.

What an artist's duty is. This is Shailendra's stated position that the essay endorses, so the मंतव्य strand C-H2.3-LO-2 rather than LO-1. Its key ('entertain the viewers') contradicts the parallel item keyed to refining the consumer's taste -- reported.
Why Indian films glorify tragic situations. A reason the passage supplies, so C-H2.3-LO-1 rather than LO-2.
When 'तीसरी कसम' reached the screen (1966). Factual recall, hence C-H2.3-LO-1.
Whose feelings Shailendra gave words to (Raj Kapoor's). Content of the essay, so C-H2.3-LO-1.
Which actress played Hirabai (Waheeda Rehman). Factual, C-H2.3-LO-1 and not LO-2.
Which film the song 'प्यार हुआ इकरार हुआ' belongs to (श्री 420). Content recall, so C-H2.3-LO-1.

Duplicate of the 'प्यार हुआ इकरार हुआ' item, mapped C-H2.3-LO-1 on the same content. Its stem has absorbed a block of textbook Q&A, its key contradicts its twin's and its answer field holds an unrelated passage -- reported.
Who wrote the lesson (प्रहलाद अग्रवाल). Authorship identification, which neither C-H2.3-LO-1 (the text's content) nor LO-2 (its writer's view and style) covers, so the competency itself.
The sad truth about the film (distributors were hard to find). A fact of the essay, so C-H2.3-LO-1.
The heroine of 'तीसरी कसम' (Waheeda Rehman). Factual recall, C-H2.3-LO-1.
Which awards the film won. Content recall, so C-H2.3-LO-1 rather than LO-2.
Which film is 'a poem written on celluloid'. The stem only asks which film the writer's phrase names, so C-H2.3-LO-1; an item asking why he calls it that would be LO-2.
Why distributors were hard to find -- it was an artistic film beyond those who count money. A reason the essay gives, hence C-H2.3-LO-1.
Why Jaikishan objected to the 'दसों दिशाओं' line. A narrated reason, so C-H2.3-LO-1 rather than the भाषा-शैली strand LO-2.
What, in Shailendra's view, an artist's duty is -- to refine the consumer's taste. The stem asks for a stated मंतव्य, so C-H2.3-LO-2 and not LO-1.
The distinguishing quality of Shailendra's songs (भाव-प्रवणता). An appraisal of language and feeling, hence C-H2.3-LO-2 rather than C-H2.3-LO-1.
Beside which river Hiraman sits and sings. Content recall about the film, so C-H2.3-LO-1. (The keyed answer 'कजरी' names a song form, not a river -- noted as a doubtful key.)
The greatest weakness of our films. Mapped C-H2.3-LO-1 on the stem's content; its answer field holds '(क) तीसरी कसम', which belongs to a different item -- reported.
What Raj Kapoor said on hearing the story (that he wanted his fee in advance). Narrative content, so C-H2.3-LO-1.
Shailendra's state on hearing Raj Kapoor (his face fell). A fact of the essay, hence C-H2.3-LO-1.
What, according to the लेखक, our films most lack. The stem explicitly asks for the writer's own judgement, so C-H2.3-LO-2, unlike the twin item that asks the same fact without naming him.
What kind of words fill this writing (the vocabulary of the film world). A remark on the author's भाषा, so C-H2.3-LO-2 rather than LO-1.
Names of Prahlad Agrawal's works. Bibliographic लेखक-परिचय, so the literature competency rather than either prose outcome.
The author's year of birth. लेखक-परिचय, hence C-H2.3.
What Raj Kapoor had not foreseen about 'मेरा नाम जोकर' (six years to finish). Content recall, so C-H2.3-LO-1.
Who wrote the lesson (प्रहलाद अग्रवाल). Authorship identification, so C-H2.3 rather than a content outcome.
Where the author was born (Jabalpur). लेखक-परिचय, hence C-H2.3.
In which subject the author took his postgraduate degree (Hindi). लेखक-परिचय, so C-H2.3.
When the film was released (1966). Content recall, C-H2.3-LO-1. (Its stem reads 'तीसरी फिल्म' for 'तीसरी कसम' -- an OCR slip, noted.)
Which four films Raj Kapoor announced together. Factual recall from the essay, so C-H2.3-LO-1.
The quality of Shailendra's songs (feeling and simplicity). An appraisal of his language, hence C-H2.3-LO-2 rather than LO-1.
Why 'तीसरी कसम' was praised. Mapped C-H2.3-LO-1 on the stem's content; its options are places (कारखाना, नौटंकी, विद्यालय) and answer none of it -- a stem/option mismatch, reported.
Where Raj Kapoor is called the greatest showman of (Asia). Content recall, so C-H2.3-LO-1.
How long one part of 'जोकर' took (six years). A fact of the essay, hence C-H2.3-LO-1.
Which remark of Raj Kapoor's made Shailendra's face fall (asking for his fee). Narrative content, so C-H2.3-LO-1.

Which poet 'तीसरी कसम' belongs to (Shailendra). An attribution item, so C-H2.3. Its options (ख) शैलेन्द्र and (ग) शैलन्द्र are the same name in two spellings and the key picks the misspelt one -- reported.
When work on 'मेरा नाम जोकर' began (1965). Content recall, hence C-H2.3-LO-1.
Whose story the film was made from (Phanishwarnath Renu's). A fact of the essay, so C-H2.3-LO-1 rather than C-H2.3, which is kept for facts about the lesson's own author.
When the author's interest in films began (in childhood). लेखक-परिचय, so the literature competency rather than the prose-content outcome.
